Summary: Semi-Pelagianism arose in southern Gaul in the 5th century as a middle position. It taught that the first step toward faith can come from human will, with God's grace then completing what the person began.
Beliefs: Humans can initiate faith on their own; God's grace cooperates with human will after the first step; Original sin weakens but does not fully corrupt the will
Controversy: Addressed at the Second Council of Orange AD 529, which affirmed that even the beginning of faith is a gift of grace
ChristianResponse: The church taught that faith itself begins by grace, pointing to Philippians 2:13 and John 6:44, while still affirming human responsibility to respond.
RelatedPeople: John Cassian; Augustine; Prosper of Aquitaine
